correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs from definitions. Orthogonal Frobenius--Schur type supplies a nonzero invariant quadratic tensor Q in Sym^2(V). Multiplication by Q is injective in the symmetric algebra, and compact-group complete reducibility gives Sym^j(V) as Sym^(j-2)(V) plus a complement of positive dimension for dim(V)>=2. Iterating yields at least floor(min(k,l)/2)+1 common nonzero summands for same-parity symmetric powers, hence the claimed Hom-space covariance floor. Prime independence then gives the tau(gcd(u,v)) square-class bound. Reindexing t=r a^2 is exact and gives the x log x + O(x) second-moment lower bound. In dimension one the parity covariance is exact. Invariant powers Q^a give nonnegative square means, and Jensen is used only where 2q>=1. The full source paper was checked: its Section 7 proves only the symmetric-square orthogonal example exactly, not this universal result.
